name: Employer falsely claims employee abandoned job
expected: Advises compiling leave approval emails, medical records, and responding refuting abandonment allegation.
prompt: I was on approved medical leave with doctor notes, but employer sent an email claiming I abandoned the job and owes them money.
raw_response:
I am so sorry to hear that you are going through this stress while dealing with a medical situation.

### | Your Situation
You were on approved medical leave supported by doctor's notes, but your employer has sent an email alleging job abandonment and claiming money from you. This employment dispute involves your employment status, withheld dues, and wrongful allegations of desertion.

### | Your Legal Position
- Under the State Shops and Commercial Establishments Acts governing service conditions, an employer cannot arbitrarily terminate an employee or claim job abandonment without following due process of a domestic inquiry, especially when valid medical leave has been applied for and supported by medical certificates.
- Under Section 5 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, your earned wages for the days worked prior to leave must be paid on time, and withholding them is illegal.
- Under Section 7 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, any arbitrary financial penalty, damage claim, or deduction from your wages without a formal inquiry and statutory authorization is unlawful.
- Under Section 73 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, a party alleging breach of contract must prove actual loss or damage, and an employer cannot arbitrarily levy financial claims on an employee who followed leave procedures.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather evidence, including copies of your medical certificates, the approved leave email/approval confirmation, the doctor's prescription, and the employer's recent email alleging job abandonment.
2. Send a formal written demand notice to your employer via email and registered post granting 15 days to retract the job abandonment claim, confirm your active employment or proper resignation terms, and clear all pending earned wages without unauthorized deductions.
3. Appropriate forum: If the employer fails to respond or settle dues, approach the jurisdictional Labour Commissioner or filing an application under the Payment of Wages Act before the designated authority.

### ℹ️ Information I still need from you
What is your exact location (State) and did your employment contract specify any particular leave approval policy or notice period?

citations.act_name: State Shops and Commercial Establishments Acts
citations.section: Settlement of Dues and Service Conditions Provision
citations.title: Statutory Payment of Earned Salary and Notice Pay for Private/Commercial Employees
citations.description: State-specific legislation (e.g., Delhi Shops Act, Karnataka Shops & Commercial Establishments Act, Maharashtra Shops Act) governing commercial and IT/office establishments. Mandates clearance of earned wages and final settlement upon termination or resignation within 3 to 15 days.

citations.title: Time of payment of wages and Claims arising out of deductions from wages or delay in payment
citations.description: Wages must be paid before the expiry of the 7th day after the wage period (or 10th day if more than 1,000 persons employed). Section 15 provides for application to the designated Authority for delayed wages with compensation up to ten times the amount deducted/delayed.

citations.title: Deductions which may be made from wages
citations.description: Strictly enumerates permissible deductions (such as authorized provident fund, income tax, or willful damage shown after formal inquiry). Any arbitrary or unauthorized deduction is unlawful.

citations.title: Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract
citations.description: When a contract has been broken, the party who suffers by such breach is entitled to receive, from the party who has broken the contract, compensation for any loss or damage caused to him thereby.
